messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: REDWOOD ALERT — elevated 5xx rate from inference-proxy in az-usw2a. Detecting spike in connection resets and target registration failures. Auto-escalate to oncall.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming impact: frontend error rate + latency up for dedicated tenant C. Any customer-facing pages affected?

cs-bot: Customer C reported increased request errors and slow responses via support ticket #4567. They see ~30% error rate on long-context prompts.

devon: seeing ENI attach failures in cloud logs for host fleet in usw2a: "AttachNetworkInterface rate limited" and repeated "NetworkInterfaceCreationError". Affected hosts failing to accept new inference containers.

sean: that matches our autoscaler logs — new nodes stuck in provisioning for ~2m, then give up. Existing nodes are healthy but traffic concentration causing kernel-level tx drops. Dumps show lots of econnreset from the NLB front.

liz: NLB metrics show target unhealthy counts rising in the same AZ. CrossZone balancing is enabled but we have sticky session routing for some inference shards. If nodes drop we get tail latency spike and retries amplify.

sam-op: quick action: divert new traffic away from usw2a. Can we flip Route53 weighted record to push 100% to us-east-1 for compute-heavy routes? TTL is 60s currently.

maya (oncall): Agree. Devon/Sean, can you confirm there are spare capacity pools in us-east-1 that can take the traffic immediately? I don't want DNS flip if we can't serve.

devon: us-east-1 has spare dedicated capacity in the pool. I can increase weights. Also we can temporarily remove the problematic target groups from the NLB in usw2a to avoid half-open connections.

sean: I'll run the NLB target deregister script. Command: ```
# deregister targets in problematic target group
aws --region us-west-2 elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/rgd-usw2a --targets Id=i-0abc1234
``` 
Expect a few seconds of 502s during connection drains.

maya (oncall): ok do it and post progress. I'll page network oncall (sam-op) to check for host-side ENI attach quotas and if AWS is reporting ENI throttle events.

sam-op: I see elevated "ENI rate-limited" events in CloudTrail. Opening support case with AWS: case 11223344 — they confirm a transient control-plane throttling in that AZ causing attach failures for ephemeral ENIs. They're estimating 30-90 min to clear.

deploy-bot: Automated canary rollback aborted (was in flight) due to inability to register new targets in usw2a.

liz: While we shift traffic, set inference-proxy retry budget lower for affected routes so we don't pile on retries. Can we set exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaker open at 20% 5xx rate?

devon: yes. Patch inbound proxy config (rolling): ```yaml
retry_policy:
  attempts: 2
  per_try_timeout: 3s
circuit_breaker:
  max_ejected: 5
  error_threshold: 0.2
``` Will rollout to control-plane within 2m.

sean: NLB targets deregistered. Healthchecks dropping to 0 for the group. Route53 weight change in flight: switching inference-weighted to us-east-1=100. Command: ```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://weights.json
``` 
Weights pushed, TTL 60. Monitor.

maya (oncall): :thumbsup: Good. CS — notify Customer C that we're actively rerouting traffic to alternate region and we expect reduced errors within 2-3 minutes due to DNS TTL.

cs-bot: Message queued to Customer C: "We observed a regional network/control-plane degradation in us-west-2a affecting inference throughput. We've routed your traffic to an alternate region and are monitoring. We'll update with ETA once AWS confirms resolution." — sent.

sean: Post-shift metrics: overall 5xx down from 28% -> 6% across the fleet; tail latency improved. A handful of sticky-session flows still hitting old AZ because of long-lived connections to inference-proxy; we should drain those hosts.

devon: starting controlled drain of remaining instances in the affected autoscaling groups. Also removing autoscaler scaling policies temporarily to avoid launching more nodes in us-west-2.

sam-op: AWS support updated: they are increasing attach quota throttle for the region and will monitor. ETA now ~40 minutes for stable throughput. They suspect control-plane API contention on host attach operations.

maya (oncall): plan summary: 1) Drain and deregister targets in usw2a. 2) Route53 weighted failover to us-east-1 (done). 3) Harden proxy retry/circuit-breaker (rolling). 4) Temporarily pause launches into usw2a until AWS clears. 5) CS notified. 6) Re-evaluate for failover-to-read replica if any stateful work impacted.

liz: We need to track cost/quota impact — moving traffic cross-region ramps egress and long-term will increase cost. Ops: add tag `incident:1767589200-eni-throttle` to the change for billing review.

devon: Adding the tag and also enabling additional KV cache warmup in us-east-1 to reduce cold-start quality regressions for real-time customers.

sean: After draining, we still see a small percentage of 504s from older connections. I'm going to force-close lingering sockets on the old hosts: ```
sudo ss -K dst 10.10.8.5 dport = :443
``` Use carefully.

maya (oncall): Coordinate time window with CS for any visible blips. We should also create a post-incident task to add regional fallback automation so we don't manually flip Route53 next time.

sam-op: AWS case updated: they will keep throttle increased until midnight UTC. They recommend avoiding heavy ENI churn in the AZ until then. I'll request an incident postmortem from AWS.

cs-bot: Customer C acknowledges the update and reports partial recovery. They will keep open ticket for 24h and want an RCA.

maya (oncall): ok team — keep monitoring for 30m. If AWS clears before then, we'll gradually move traffic back with a canary. Assign follow-ups: devon -> Runbook update for ENI throttle detection; liz -> Add fallback automation spec; sean -> socket-drain script enhancements; sam-op -> AWS postmortem request. I'll convert thread to incident channel summary in 15m.

deploy-bot: rollback of the aborted canary scheduled for 10:15 UTC if we confirm all targets healthy in us-east-1.

sean: Metrics look stable: 5xx floor ~2-4% (normal). Leaving NLB drain in place for 10 minutes then terminate instances.

maya (oncall): closing hands-on for now. If any regression, re-open channel. Great job everyone. :heart:
